title: Golden Retrievers Were Never Russian Circus Dogs
description:
A golden retriever made the news this week for leaping into a pool to save a toddler. For decades, people claimed the breed came from Russian circus dogs bought in Brighton. The kennel records tell a different story, and it starts on a Highland estate called Guisachan.

🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:00 A golden retriever in the news
0:09 The legend: Russian circus dogs
0:13 The records: Guisachan, Scotland
0:25 A yellow pup from a black litter
0:30 Nous
0:32 1868: Nous and Belle, a Tweed Water Spaniel
0:37 Crocus, Cowslip, Primrose and Ada
0:42 How the legend was put to rest
0:47 Golden Retrievers, 1920 and 1932
0:54 Bred for the water

A note on dates: sources disagree on whether Marjoribanks got Nous in 1865 or 1868, so the video says "the 1860s". The cobbler and circus tales about Nous's origin are legends; Lord Tweedmouth's stud book records him as bred near Brighton.

Images: Nous at Guisachan, 1870s, and Winifred Charlesworth with golden retrievers, 1910s (Wikimedia Commons, public domain). Guisachan, Inverness-shire, from "Edward Marjoribanks, Lord Tweedmouth, 1849-1909: Notes and Recollections" (Constable, 1909), via the Internet Archive. Flat-coated retriever engraving from Vero Shaw, "The Illustrated Book of the Dog" (Cassell, 1881), via the Internet Archive. Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) and US Census (us-atlas) outlines.
Sources: Golden Retriever Club of America breed history; Wikipedia, "Golden Retriever" and "Dudley Marjoribanks, 1st Baron Tweedmouth".
Narration voice is synthetic.
